_meta.description: Perturbation methods and actuators, with the valence a given actuator canonically implies.
valence_policy: canonical_valence is the valence the ACTUATOR implies when used as designed, and matches the SCHEMA.md 3.4 enum (activation, inhibition, ablation, unclear).

It is a prior, not a verdict. A paper's actual valence field must come from the paper. Example: hM4Di in a neuron whose output is itself inhibitory produces net downstream activation; the record still says inhibition for the perturbation and the circuit interpretation lives elsewhere.

unclear is used wherever the net effect on the targeted population genuinely depends on context: electrical stimulation, lesion, tetanus toxin, conditional knockout, conditional overexpression and local pharmacology.
_meta.method_enum_note: 'method' values are the SCHEMA.md 3.4 enum: optogenetic, chemogenetic, electrical_stimulation, lesion, genetic_ablation, conditional_knockout, conditional_overexpression, local_pharmacology, other.

optogenetic_unspecified.notes: For papers that say only 'optogenetic' without naming the opsin. Valence is unclear BY CONSTRUCTION here: the actuator decides it, and we do not know the actuator. Also the generic-term block used for literature search.

synonyms: designer receptor exclusively activated by designer drugs
chemogenetic_unspecified.notes: For papers that say only 'chemogenetic'/'DREADD' without naming the receptor. Valence unclear by construction, as above.

ablation_unspecified.notes: For papers reporting ablation without naming the construct. Valence is ablation because cell loss is the stated intent, but the construct and its completeness are unknown.

opto_chr2.notes: Blue-light cation channel. Includes faster/high-photocurrent variants. Frequency, pulse width and power must be captured; high-frequency drive can depolarisation-block, which is the main way ChR2 produces a non-activating effect.

opto_enphr.notes: Chloride pump. Prolonged use shifts the chloride gradient and can paradoxically increase excitability on light-off rebound.

opto_archt.notes: Proton pump. Alkalinises terminals and can increase spontaneous release, a known confound for terminal inhibition.

opto_gtacr.notes: Anion channelrhodopsin. At axon terminals GtACRs can be excitatory because of the local chloride gradient.

chemo_hm3dq.notes: Ligands in use are CNO, deschloroclozapine (DCZ) and compound 21 (C21); CNO back-metabolises to clozapine, so a ligand-in-non-expressing control is required for the record to be interpretable.

chemo_hm4di.notes: Gi-coupled; also suppresses terminal release independently of somatic silencing. Same ligand caveats as hM3Dq.

chemo_kord.notes: Gi-coupled, orthogonal ligand to CNO so it is used for sequential bidirectional designs.

chemo_gq_other.notes: Bucket for papers that name only the coupling, not the receptor variant.

ablation_casp3.notes: AAV-flex-Casp3-TEVp is the usual Cre-dependent construct. Ablation is partial and must be quantified in the paper to be usable.

ablation_dta.notes: Cell-autonomous, usually constitutive from the time of Cre expression, so developmental compensation is a real confound for chronic phenotypes.

ablation_dtr.notes: Timed version of DTA; the inducing ligand is diphtheria toxin itself.

ablation_toxin_chemical.notes: Chemically specific only in a loose sense; selectivity claims must come from the paper's own histology. Classed as lesion with ablation valence because cell loss is the intended effect.

lesion_electrolytic.notes: Destroys cell bodies, passing fibres and local glia indiscriminately, so the net effect on any one population is not determinable: valence unclear even though tissue is destroyed.

electrical_stimulation.notes: Activates cell bodies, afferents and fibres of passage; high-frequency DBS can functionally inhibit. Valence genuinely unclear.

tetx.notes: Blocks vesicular release while leaving the cell electrically alive and peptide release partly intact (peptides use large dense-core vesicles with different SNARE dependence). Net effect on the population's output is therefore unclear, not a clean inhibition.

conditional_knockout.notes: Deleting a gene can raise or lower the excitability and output of the population depending on the gene, so valence is unclear by default and must be taken from the paper's own functional data if any.

local_pharmacology.notes: Receptor-level, not cell-type level, and the affected cell population is defined only by diffusion. Valence unclear; also frequently fails the population-specificity requirement for a Tier A record.

opto_terminal.notes: Bucket for projection-specific designs; the opsin identity determines the real valence, so record both this and the opsin entry. Flagged unclear because terminal manipulation can antidromically drive or inhibit the soma population.

thermogenetic.notes: Heterogeneous and methodologically contested family (magnetogenetics in particular). Grouped as activation because that is the intended use, with low curation certainty; treat records from here sceptically.
